northern-cardinal._en_desc: The northern cardinal is a vivid red songbird with a distinctive crest and black face. Males are brilliant red while females are warm brown with red accents.

blue-jay._en_desc: The blue jay is a striking songbird with blue, white, and black plumage and a prominent crest. It is intelligent and vocal, known for its loud calls and bold behavior.

american-crow._en_desc: The American crow is a large, all-black bird known for its intelligence and adaptability. It uses tools, solves complex problems, and lives in large family groups.

common-raven._en_desc: The common raven is the largest songbird in North America. Extremely intelligent, it has been observed using tools, solving multi-step puzzles, and manipulating other animals.

house-sparrow._en_desc: The house sparrow is one of the most widespread and familiar birds in the world. Originally from Eurasia, it thrives in close association with human habitation.

european-robin._en_desc: The European robin is a small insectivorous bird with a distinctive orange-red breast. Familiar in gardens across Europe, it is known for its territorial behavior.

eastern-bluebird._en_desc: The eastern bluebird is a small thrush with brilliant blue plumage on the back and a rusty-red throat and breast. A symbol of happiness, it was saved from decline by nest box programs.

western-bluebird._en_desc: The western bluebird is a small thrush with deep blue plumage and a rusty breast. It nests in cavities and feeds primarily on insects caught on the ground.

baltimore-oriole._en_desc: The Baltimore oriole is a striking songbird with vivid orange and black plumage. They weave elaborate pendulous nests from plant fibers.

scarlet-tanager._en_desc: The scarlet tanager is a medium-sized songbird with brilliant red plumage and black wings during breeding season. It is a shy forest bird.

yellow-warbler._en_desc: The yellow warbler is a small, bright yellow songbird widespread across North America. Its cheerful song is one of the most recognizable spring sounds.

white-throated-sparrow._en_desc: The white-throated sparrow is a common songbird with a distinctive white throat patch and yellow lores. It has two color morphs that differ in behavior.

dark-eyed-junco._en_desc: The dark-eyed junco is a small, slate-colored sparrow common across North America. It is one of the most abundant and widespread forest birds.

ruby-throated-hummingbird._en_desc: The ruby-throated hummingbird is the only breeding hummingbird in eastern North America. Males have an iridescent ruby-red throat.

annas-hummingbird._en_desc: Annas hummingbird is a small, green hummingbird native to western North America. Males have a brilliant rose-pink throat and crown.

black-chinned-hummingbird._en_desc: The black-chinned hummingbird is a small, common hummingbird of the western United States with a velvet-black chin that shows iridescent purple.

belted-kingfisher._en_desc: The belted kingfisher is a stocky, blue-gray bird with a shaggy crest and large dagger-like bill. Females have an additional rusty band across the belly.

great-blue-heron._en_desc: The great blue heron is the largest heron in North America, with a wingspan up to 6.5 feet. It wades in shallow water to hunt fish.

great-egret._en_desc: The great egret is a large, all-white heron with a yellow bill and black legs. Its near-extinction for the millinery trade helped spark the conservation movement.

snowy-egret._en_desc: The snowy egret is a small, elegant white heron with black legs and vivid yellow feet. During breeding season, it develops long, flowing plumes.

green-heron._en_desc: The green heron is a small, stocky heron with dark greenish-gray plumage. It is a clever hunter that sometimes uses bait to lure fish.

flamingo._en_desc: The greater flamingo is the largest and most widespread flamingo species. Its pink plumage, long legs, and curved bill are unmistakable.

american-flamingo._en_desc: The American flamingo is a large, bright pink wading bird found in the Caribbean and Galapagos with the brightest plumage of all flamingos.

sandhill-crane._en_desc: The sandhill crane is a tall, gray bird with a red crown and long legs. Known for its trumpeting call and spectacular mating dances.

whooping-crane._en_desc: The whooping crane is the tallest bird in North America. Named for its loud whooping call, it was saved from extinction through intensive conservation.

purple-gallinule._en_desc: The purple gallinule is a brightly colored marsh bird with purple-blue plumage and a red and yellow bill. It walks gracefully on floating vegetation.

american-coot._en_desc: The American coot is a dark, chicken-like waterbird with a white bill and frontal shield. Despite looking duck-like, it is related to rails.

wild-turkey._en_desc: The wild turkey is a large, iridescent bird native to North America. Males display elaborate courtship rituals. It is the ancestor of the domesticated turkey.

ring-necked-pheasant._en_desc: The ring-necked pheasant is a colorful game bird originally from Asia, now established across North America and Europe. Males have brilliant copper and green plumage.

bobwhite-quail._en_desc: The northern bobwhite is a small, compact quail with a distinctive white throat and eyebrow stripe in males. Named for its clear bob-white call.

california-quail._en_desc: The California quail is a small, plump ground bird with a distinctive forward-curving black head plume. It is the state bird of California.

ostrich._en_desc: The common ostrich is the largest living bird, native to Africa. Unable to fly, it has powerful legs and can run at sustained speeds of 30 mph.

rockhopper-penguin._en_desc: The rockhopper penguin is a small penguin known for its distinctive yellow and black crest feathers. It navigates steep, rocky terrain by hopping.

little-blue-penguin._en_desc: The little blue penguin, also known as the fairy penguin, is the smallest species of penguin. Found in New Zealand and southern Australia.

gentoo-penguin._en_desc: The gentoo penguin is recognizable by the white stripe across its head and its bright orange-red bill. It is the fastest underwater swimming bird.

african-penguin._en_desc: The African penguin, also known as the jackass penguin for its donkey-like bray, is the only penguin species that breeds in Africa. It is endangered.

brown-kiwi._en_desc: The brown kiwi is a flightless bird native to New Zealand. It has hair-like feathers, no tail, and a long probing bill with nostrils at the tip.

lyrebird._en_desc: The superb lyrebird is famous for its extraordinary ability to mimic sounds. Males have an elaborate tail that forms a lyre shape during courtship.

cassowary._en_desc: The southern cassowary is a large, flightless bird with a distinctive blue neck, red wattles, and a bony casque on its head.

scarlet-macaw._en_desc: The scarlet macaw is a large, colorful parrot with brilliant red, yellow, and blue plumage. Found in Central and South American rainforests.

blue-and-yellow-macaw._en_desc: The blue-and-yellow macaw is a large parrot with vivid blue upperparts and golden-yellow underparts. It is highly social and can mimic human speech.

hyacinth-macaw._en_desc: The hyacinth macaw is the largest of all flying parrot species, with stunning cobalt-blue plumage and bright yellow eye rings.

african-grey-parrot._en_desc: The African grey parrot is renowned for its exceptional intelligence and ability to mimic human speech. It has grey plumage with a striking red tail.

budgerigar._en_desc: The budgerigar is a small, long-tailed parakeet native to Australia. In the wild, it is green and yellow with black markings.

cockatiel._en_desc: The cockatiel is a small parrot native to Australia, recognizable by its prominent crest and orange cheek patches.

keel-billed-toucan._en_desc: The keel-billed toucan is a colorful bird with a massive, rainbow-colored bill. Found in Central and South American rainforests.

toco-toucan._en_desc: The toco toucan is the largest toucan species, with a massive orange-yellow bill tipped in black. Found in South American forests.

great-hornbill._en_desc: The great hornbill is one of the largest hornbill species, distinguished by its massive yellow and black casque atop its bill.

rhinoceros-hornbill._en_desc: The rhinoceros hornbill is a large hornbill with a dramatic upward-curving casque on its bill. Found in Southeast Asian rainforests.

laughing-kookaburra._en_desc: The laughing kookaburra is a large kingfisher native to Australia, famous for its distinctive call that sounds like loud, echoing human laughter.

pied-kingfisher._en_desc: The pied kingfisher is a black and white kingfisher found across Africa and Asia. It hovers over water before diving to catch fish.

atlantic-puffin._en_desc: The Atlantic puffin is a small seabird with a colorful triangular bill and distinctive black and white plumage. Known as the clown of the sea.

tufted-puffin._en_desc: The tufted puffin is a small seabird with black plumage, white face patches, and distinctive golden head tufts during breeding season.

wandering-albatross._en_desc: The wandering albatross has the largest wingspan of any bird, up to 11.5 feet. It spends most of its life soaring over the Southern Ocean.

black-browed-albatross._en_desc: The black-browed albatross is a large seabird with dark upper wings and a white body. Named for the dark stripe through its eye.

laysan-albatross._en_desc: The Laysan albatross is a large seabird of the North Pacific. It breeds primarily on remote Pacific islands.

brown-pelican._en_desc: The brown pelican is a large waterbird with a massive bill and throat pouch. It is unique among pelicans for plunge-diving from the air.

american-white-pelican._en_desc: The American white pelican is one of the largest North American birds, with a wingspan up to 9 feet. It scoops fish while swimming.

frigatebird._en_desc: The magnificent frigatebird is a large seabird with long, angular wings and a deeply forked tail. Males inflate a bright red throat pouch.

northern-gannet._en_desc: The northern gannet is the largest seabird in the North Atlantic. It nests in massive colonies on sea cliffs.

blue-footed-booby._en_desc: The blue-footed booby is a marine bird famous for its vivid blue feet. Found along the Pacific coast of the Americas.

red-footed-booby._en_desc: The red-footed booby is the smallest booby species, with distinctive red feet. It comes in several color morphs.

great-cormorant._en_desc: The great cormorant is a large, dark waterbird found across much of the world. It spreads its wings to dry after fishing.

common-loon._en_desc: The common loon is a large waterbird known for its haunting wail across northern lakes. Its solid bones help it dive deep.

arctic-tern._en_desc: The Arctic tern migrates farther than any other animal. It experiences more daylight than any other creature.

caspian-tern._en_desc: The Caspian tern is the worlds largest tern, with a massive red bill and black cap. Found on every continent except Antarctica.

black-skimmer._en_desc: The black skimmer is a unique seabird with a distinctive uneven bill. It flies low over water, dragging its bill to catch fish.

herring-gull._en_desc: The herring gull is one of the most common gulls in the Northern Hemisphere, thriving in coastal and urban environments.

laughing-gull._en_desc: The laughing gull is a medium-sized gull with a distinctive black head in breeding season and a laughing call.

killdeer._en_desc: The killdeer is a large plover with distinctive black breast bands. It is famous for its broken-wing display.

american-woodcock._en_desc: The American woodcock is a plump shorebird with a long bill. It feeds on earthworms and performs an aerial sky-dance at dusk.

red-knot._en_desc: The red knot is famous for one of the longest migrations in the animal kingdom. It turns rusty-red during breeding season.

american-avocet._en_desc: The American avocet is an elegant wader with a thin, upturned bill and long legs. During breeding season, its head and neck turn rusty-orange.

black-necked-stilt._en_desc: The black-necked stilt is a striking wader with black upperparts, white underparts, and extraordinarily long pink legs.

willow-ptarmigan._en_desc: The willow ptarmigan is a game bird of the Arctic tundra that changes plumage with the seasons.

spruce-grouse._en_desc: The spruce grouse is a forest-dwelling game bird of the boreal region, known for its tameness.

ruffed-grouse._en_desc: The ruffed grouse is a popular game bird of eastern North American forests with a distinctive drumming display.

chukar._en_desc: The chukar is a rotund game bird native to Eurasia and introduced to North America with distinctive black and white barring.

common-crane._en_desc: The common crane is a large, elegant wading bird with gray plumage and a red crown patch. Famous for its courtship dances.

demoiselle-crane._en_desc: The demoiselle crane is the smallest crane species, elegant and graceful with a black neck and white ear tufts.

bearded-vulture._en_desc: The bearded vulture is the only bird species that feeds almost exclusively on bones.

andean-condor._en_desc: The Andean condor is one of the worlds largest flying birds. It soars on thermal currents over the Andes mountains.

king-vulture._en_desc: The king vulture is a large, colorful vulture with a vividly colored head and a white body.

turkey-vulture._en_desc: The turkey vulture is a large soaring bird with a red, featherless head resembling a wild turkey.

american-kestrel._en_desc: The American kestrel is the smallest and most common falcon in North America. Males have slate-blue wings.

merlin._en_desc: The merlin is a small, powerful falcon found across the Northern Hemisphere. It pursues small birds in direct flight.

prairie-falcon._en_desc: The prairie falcon is a large, sandy-brown falcon of the western North American open country.

gyrfalcon._en_desc: The gyrfalcon is the largest of all falcon species, found in Arctic regions. It was historically prized in falconry for royalty.

osprey._en_desc: The osprey is a large raptor found on every continent except Antarctica. It feeds almost exclusively on fish.

northern-harrier._en_desc: The northern harrier is a slim raptor that hunts by flying low over open ground, using both sight and sound.

coopers-hawk._en_desc: The Coopers hawk is a medium-sized accipiter that specializes in capturing doves and songbirds in flight.

sharp-shinned-hawk._en_desc: The sharp-shinned hawk is the smallest accipiter in North America. A rapid, agile flier that hunts small songbirds.

swainsons-hawk._en_desc: The Swainsons hawk is a medium-sized raptor that migrates in enormous flocks to the pampas of Argentina for the winter.

rough-legged-hawk._en_desc: The rough-legged hawk breeds in the Arctic tundra and winters in open prairies of North America.

ferruginous-hawk._en_desc: The ferruginous hawk is the largest buteo hawk in North America with rust-colored upperparts.

white-tailed-kite._en_desc: The white-tailed kite is a graceful raptor with white plumage, black shoulders, and a forked tail.

mississippi-kite._en_desc: The Mississippi kite is a small, elegant raptor with pearl-gray plumage that feeds primarily on insects caught in flight.

red-winged-blackbird._en_desc: The red-winged blackbird is one of the most abundant and widespread birds in North America with bright red and yellow shoulder patches.

brown-headed-cowbird._en_desc: The brown-headed cowbird is a brood parasite that lays its eggs in the nests of other bird species.

common-grackle._en_desc: The common grackle is a large, lanky blackbird with iridescent plumage and bright yellow eyes.

great-tailed-grackle._en_desc: The great-tailed grackle is a large, noisy blackbird with a very long, keel-shaped tail.

yellow-headed-blackbird._en_desc: The yellow-headed blackbird is a striking songbird with a brilliant yellow-orange head contrasting with a black body.

eastern-meadowlark._en_desc: The eastern meadowlark is a bright yellow songbird with a distinctive V-shaped black breast band.

western-meadowlark._en_desc: The western meadowlark is a bright yellow songbird with a black V-shaped breast band, the state bird of six states.

orchard-oriole._en_desc: The orchard oriole is a small, chestnut and black songbird. Males have a chestnut body with a black head.

bullocks-oriole._en_desc: The Bullocks oriole is a bright orange and black songbird of western North America that weaves hanging basket nests.

barn-swallow._en_desc: The barn swallow is the most widespread swallow species in the world with a distinctive deeply forked tail.

tree-swallow._en_desc: The tree swallow is a small, iridescent blue-green swallow with white underparts.

cliff-swallow._en_desc: The cliff swallow is a small swallow with a pale rump and squared-off tail that builds enclosed mud nests in colonies.

purple-martin._en_desc: The purple martin is the largest North American swallow with iridescent purple-blue plumage in males.

bank-swallow._en_desc: The bank swallow is the smallest swallow in North America, nesting in burrows excavated in sandy banks near water.

violet-green-swallow._en_desc: The violet-green swallow is a small, colorful swallow with iridescent green and violet upperparts.

chimney-swift._en_desc: The chimney swift is a cigar-shaped, dark gray bird that spends most of its life on the wing.

common-nighthawk._en_desc: The common nighthawk is a nocturnal bird that feeds on flying insects caught during acrobatic aerial displays.

eastern-whip-poor-will._en_desc: The eastern whip-poor-will is a nocturnal bird named for its distinctive three-part call.

greater-roadrunner._en_desc: The greater roadrunner is a large, ground-dwelling cuckoo of the American deserts known for its X-shaped tail.

yellow-billed-cuckoo._en_desc: The yellow-billed cuckoo is a slim, long-tailed bird with a curved yellow bill that feeds on caterpillars.

hoopoe._en_desc: The Eurasian hoopoe is a distinctive bird with cinnamon plumage, black and white wing bars, and a spectacular erectile crest.

tawny-frogmouth._en_desc: The tawny frogmouth is a nocturnal bird of Australia with cryptic plumage that perfectly camouflages it against tree bark.

common-potoo._en_desc: The common potoo is a nocturnal bird of Central and South American forests with an enormous mouth and cryptic plumage.

american-goldfinch._en_desc: The American goldfinch is a small, bright yellow songbird with black wings and cap, one of the latest-nesting birds in North America.

pine-grosbeak._en_desc: The pine grosbeak is a large, plump finch with rosy-pink plumage in males. Found in boreal forests across North America.

evening-grosbeak._en_desc: The evening grosbeak is a large, stocky finch with a massive conical bill and bright yellow body in males.

cassins-finch._en_desc: The Cassins finch is a medium-sized finch with rosy-red crown and pinkish wash on the breast, found in mountain forests.

red-crossbill._en_desc: The red crossbill is a finch with a uniquely crossed bill adapted for extracting seeds from conifer cones.

pine-siskin._en_desc: The pine siskin is a small, streaky brown finch with yellow edging on its wings and tail, an irruptive species.

common-redpoll._en_desc: The common redpoll is a tiny, streaky finch with a distinctive red cap and pink breast, breeding in Arctic tundra.

hoary-redpoll._en_desc: The hoary redpoll is a tiny Arctic finch, paler and frostier-looking than the common redpoll.

house-finch._en_desc: The house finch is a small songbird common in urban and suburban areas with red or orange plumage in males.

purple-finch._en_desc: The purple finch is a medium-sized finch with rosy-red plumage in males and streaked brown in females.

eastern-wood-pewee._en_desc: The eastern wood-pewee is a small flycatcher with olive-gray plumage and a distinctive, plaintive whistle.

great-crested-flycatcher._en_desc: The great crested flycatcher is a large, yellow-bellied flycatcher with a distinctive crest. It always includes snakeskin in its nest.

eastern-kingbird._en_desc: The eastern kingbird is a bold flycatcher with dark gray upperparts and a distinctive white tip on its tail.

eastern-phoebe._en_desc: The eastern phoebe is a small, brownish-gray flycatcher that bobs its tail frequently and often nests on human structures.

willow-flycatcher._en_desc: The willow flycatcher is a small, inconspicuous flycatcher best known for its distinctive fitz-bew song.

scissor-tailed-flycatcher._en_desc: The scissor-tailed flycatcher is a distinctive flycatcher with extremely long, forked tail feathers. It is the state bird of Oklahoma.

vermilion-flycatcher._en_desc: The vermilion flycatcher is a small, vividly colored flycatcher with males displaying brilliant red plumage and a black mask.

common-merganser._en_desc: The common merganser is a large diving duck with a reddish-brown crested head in females and a dark green head in males. It feeds primarily on fish.

hooded-merganser._en_desc: The hooded merganser is a small, striking diving duck. Males have a bold black and white fan-shaped crest with a rusty flank patch.

bufflehead._en_desc: The bufflehead is a small, compact diving duck. Males have a striking iridescent green and purple head with large white patches.

common-goldeneye._en_desc: The common goldeneye is a medium-sized diving duck with a distinctive round head. Males have a dark green-black head with a white circular patch near the bill.

ring-necked-duck._en_desc: The ring-necked duck is a medium-sized diving duck with a distinctive peaked head shape. Males have a black back, gray flanks, and a white breast with a subtle neck ring.

gadwall._en_desc: The gadwall is a dabbling duck with subtle but elegant plumage. Males are mostly gray with black rear ends, while females are mottled brown.

blue-winged-teal._en_desc: The blue-winged teal is a small dabbling duck. Males have a slate-blue head with a white crescent in front of the eye. It is one of the earliest migrating ducks.

crested-caracara._en_desc: The crested caracara is a distinctive raptor with a black cap, white neck, and orange face. Despite being in the falcon family, it scavenges and forages on the ground.

palm-nut-vulture._en_desc: The palm-nut vulture is a unique raptor of West African palm forests that feeds mainly on the fruit of the oil palm.

black-vulture._en_desc: The black vulture is a common New World vulture with black plumage and a bare, dark head. It soars in groups looking for carcasses.

roseate-spoonbill._en_desc: The roseate spoonbill is a large, pink wading bird with a distinctive spatulate bill. It feeds by sweeping its bill through shallow water.

wood-stork._en_desc: The wood stork is a large, white wading bird with a dark, featherless head and a long, curved bill. It is the only stork species breeding in the United States.

white-ibis._en_desc: The white ibis is a medium-sized wading bird with white plumage, black wing tips, and a distinctive long, curved pink bill.

limpkin._en_desc: The limpkin is a large, brown wading bird with white spotting. It is specialized in feeding on apple snails and has a distinctive wailing call.

rusty-blackbird._en_desc: The rusty blackbird is a medium-sized blackbird that breeds in boreal wetlands and winters in the southeastern United States. Males are glossy black with rust-colored edges on feathers in fall.

clownfish._en_desc: Clownfish are vibrant orange fish with white bands that live symbiotically among sea anemone tentacles. They gain protection from predators while providing the anemone with food scraps and increased water circulation.

blue-tang._en_desc: The blue tang is a striking royal blue fish with a bright yellow tail and black markings. Found throughout the Indo-Pacific, it feeds primarily on algae and plays an important role in keeping coral reefs healthy.

mandarinfish._en_desc: The mandarinfish is a small, incredibly colorful reef fish with vivid blue, orange, and green patterns. It produces a toxic mucus coating that deters predators and gives it a distinctive smell.

sixbar-wrasse._en_desc: The sixbar wrasse is a slender reef fish with distinctive dark vertical bars across its body. Found throughout the Indo-Pacific, it feeds on small crustaceans and fish.

yellowtail-coris._en_desc: The yellowtail coris is a colorful wrasse found in coral reefs across the Indo-Pacific. Adults have a green body with yellow tail and red spots, while juveniles are orange.

bicolor-angelfish._en_desc: The bicolor angelfish features a striking split coloration of dark blue-black on the front half and bright yellow on the rear half. Found in Caribbean reefs, it feeds on algae.

flame-angelfish._en_desc: The flame angelfish is a brilliant orange-red fish with black vertical bars native to the Pacific. It is one of the most popular marine aquarium fish.

queen-angelfish._en_desc: The queen angelfish is a large, stunningly colorful reef fish with blue, yellow, and green hues. Found throughout the tropical western Atlantic, it feeds primarily on sponges.

french-angelfish._en_desc: The French angelfish is a striking black fish with bright yellow-edged scales found in Caribbean reefs. Young individuals are bright yellow but darken as adults.

regal-tang._en_desc: The regal tang, also known as the palette surgeonfish, is a bright blue fish with a yellow tail and black markings. Found across the Indo-Pacific.

sohal-surgeonfish._en_desc: The sohal surgeonfish is a large, gray-blue reef fish with horizontal stripes and sharp scalpel-like spines on its tail. Native to the Red Sea and Persian Gulf.

moorish-idol._en_desc: The Moorish idol is one of the most recognizable reef fish with its dramatic black, white, and yellow coloration and a long flowing dorsal fin filament.

royal-gramma._en_desc: The royal gramma, or fairy basslet, has a stunning two-tone coloration with bright purple on the front half and yellow on the rear half. Found in Caribbean caves.

longnose-butterflyfish._en_desc: The longnose butterflyfish is a slender reef fish with a distinctive elongated snout and yellow body with a dark eye band.

copperband-butterflyfish._en_desc: The copperband butterflyfish has a striking pattern of vertical orange bands with black edges on a silver-white body.

foureye-butterflyfish._en_desc: The foureye butterflyfish gets its name from the prominent black eye spot on each side near its tail, confusing predators.

bluegill._en_desc: The bluegill is a freshwater sunfish native to eastern North America. It has an olive-green body with a distinctive dark spot on the ear flap.

largemouth-bass._en_desc: The largemouth bass is the largest of the black basses and the most popular freshwater game fish in North America.

smallmouth-bass._en_desc: The smallmouth bass is a freshwater fish prized by anglers for its aggressive fighting style.

rainbow-trout._en_desc: The rainbow trout is a coldwater fish with an olive-green body and a distinctive pinkish-red stripe along its side.

brook-trout._en_desc: The brook trout, also called speckled trout, has a dark green body with light spots and red spots with blue halos.

atlantic-salmon._en_desc: The Atlantic salmon is an anadromous fish born in freshwater, migrates to the ocean, and returns to freshwater to spawn.

chinook-salmon._en_desc: The Chinook salmon, also called king salmon, is the largest Pacific salmon with a greenish back and dark spots.

coho-salmon._en_desc: The coho salmon, also known as silver salmon, has a silver body with black spots and is found throughout the North Pacific.

pacific-bluefin-tuna._en_desc: The Pacific bluefin tuna is a large, fast, pelagic fish found throughout the Pacific Ocean, highly prized in sushi markets.

yellowfin-tuna._en_desc: The yellowfin tuna is a large, streamlined ocean fish with bright yellow dorsal and anal fins found in tropical oceans worldwide.

atlantic-cod._en_desc: The Atlantic cod is a large, cold-water fish with a distinctive chin barbel and three dorsal fins, once one of the most important food fish in the world.

atlantic-grouper._en_desc: The Atlantic grouper is a large, robust reef fish with a wide mouth and thick lips found in warm Atlantic waters.

goliath-grouper._en_desc: The goliath grouper is the largest bony fish in the Western Atlantic, reaching weights of up to 800 pounds.

red-snapper._en_desc: The red snapper is a bright red reef fish found in the Gulf of Mexico and western Atlantic.

barracuda._en_desc: The barracuda is a large, predatory fish with a long, streamlined body and razor-sharp teeth found in tropical oceans.

mahi-mahi._en_desc: The mahi-mahi is a brightly colored pelagic fish with a golden-green body and blue fins found in tropical oceans.

wahoo._en_desc: The wahoo is a large, fast pelagic fish related to mackerels with a sleek, torpedo-shaped body and vertical blue bars.

sailfish._en_desc: The sailfish is a large billfish with a spectacular high dorsal fin resembling a sail, found in tropical oceans worldwide.

blue-marlin._en_desc: The blue marlin is one of the largest ocean fish with a distinctive blue upper body and silver-white belly found in tropical Atlantic waters.

nassau-grouper._en_desc: The Nassau grouper is a large reef fish capable of rapid color changes, now critically endangered from overfishing.

striped-bass._en_desc: The striped bass is a silver fish with distinctive horizontal dark stripes found along the Atlantic coast.

red-drum._en_desc: The red drum, also called redfish, is a copper-bronze fish with a distinctive black spot near the tail.

black-drum._en_desc: The black drum is a large, dark fish with barbels on its chin that can grow to over 100 pounds.

channel-catfish._en_desc: The channel catfish is the most fished catfish species in North America with a forked tail and whisker-like barbels.

blue-catfish._en_desc: The blue catfish is the largest species of North American catfish reaching weights of over 100 pounds.

walking-catfish._en_desc: The walking catfish is a freshwater catfish native to Southeast Asia that can breathe air and move across land.

wels-catfish._en_desc: The wels catfish is the largest freshwater fish in Europe reaching lengths of over 16 feet with a wide, flat head.

eurasian-pike._en_desc: The Eurasian pike is a large, ambush predator found throughout Europe, Asia, and northern North America.

muskellunge._en_desc: The muskellunge, or muskie, is the largest freshwater fish in the pike family found in clear lakes and rivers of North America.

walleye._en_desc: The walleye is a freshwater fish named for its distinctive, glassy eyes that reflect light found in cool, clear lakes.

common-carp._en_desc: The common carp is a large, golden-brown freshwater fish found throughout the world, originally from Eurasia.

grass-carp._en_desc: The grass carp is a large freshwater fish native to eastern Asia that feeds almost exclusively on aquatic plants.

koi-carp._en_desc: Koi are ornamental varieties of common carp bred for their vibrant colors and patterns from Japan.

goldfish._en_desc: The goldfish is one of the most popular aquarium fish in the world, domesticated from East Asia over 1,000 years ago.

tench._en_desc: The tench is a freshwater fish with a thick, slimy body and olive-green to bronze coloration found throughout Europe and Asia.

three-spined-stickleback._en_desc: The three-spined stickleback is a small, spiny fish found throughout the Northern Hemisphere, males build intricate nests.

florida-gar._en_desc: The Florida gar is a long, slender predatory fish with an elongated snout and armored scales found in Florida and Georgia.

alligator-gar._en_desc: The alligator gar is the largest freshwater fish in North America, reaching over 8 feet long with a long, alligator-like snout.

bowfin._en_desc: The bowfin is a primitive freshwater fish with an elongated body and a distinctive long dorsal fin found in eastern North America.

chinese-sturgeon._en_desc: The Chinese sturgeon is a critically endangered species found only in the Yangtze River that can grow to over 16 feet.

atlantic-sturgeon._en_desc: The Atlantic sturgeon is a large, primitive fish with a prehistoric appearance featuring bony plates instead of scales.

arctic-char._en_desc: The Arctic char is a cold-water fish related to salmon and trout found in Arctic and subarctic waters.

lake-trout._en_desc: The lake trout is a large, cold-water salmonid found in deep lakes of northern North America with a forked tail.

cutthroat-trout._en_desc: The cutthroat trout is a cold-water fish native to western North America, named for red-orange slash marks under its lower jaw.

golden-trout._en_desc: The golden trout is a subspecies of rainbow trout found in high-altitude mountain streams of California with golden-yellow body.

oceanic-whitetip-shark._en_desc: The oceanic whitetip shark is a large, slow-moving pelagic shark with distinctive white-tipped fins, critically endangered.

blacktip-shark._en_desc: The blacktip shark is a medium-sized shark with distinctive black tips on all its fins found in warm coastal waters.

scalloped-hammerhead._en_desc: The scalloped hammerhead is one of the most common hammerhead species with a distinctive scalloped leading edge on its head.

thresher-shark._en_desc: The thresher shark is a distinctive shark with an extremely long upper tail that can be as long as its body found in open ocean.

basking-shark._en_desc: The basking shark is the second largest fish in the world, filter-feeding on plankton with an enormous mouth over 3 feet wide.

nurse-shark._en_desc: The nurse shark is a sluggish, bottom-dwelling shark with barbels near its nostrils that help detect prey hidden in sand.

zebra-shark._en_desc: The zebra shark is a distinctive shark with dark spots on a tan body found on tropical coral reefs of the Indo-Pacific.

epaulette-shark._en_desc: The epaulette shark is a small reef shark that can walk on its fins across the reef flat found in the Indo-Pacific.

angel-shark._en_desc: The angel shark is a flattened shark that lies buried in sand on the ocean floor, critically endangered due to habitat loss.

southern-stingray._en_desc: The southern stingray is a large, diamond-shaped ray found in shallow tropical waters of the western Atlantic.

cownose-ray._en_desc: The cownose ray is a distinctive ray with a unique head shape resembling a cow's nose, forming large schools during migration.

eagle-ray._en_desc: The spotted eagle ray is a large ray with distinctive white spots on a dark body found in tropical and subtropical oceans.

viperfish._en_desc: The viperfish is a deep-sea predator with extremely long, needle-like teeth and a bioluminescent photophore along its body.

gulper-eel._en_desc: The gulper eel is a deep-sea fish with an enormous, loosely hinged mouth and a long, whip-like tail found in deep ocean waters.

pufferfish._en_desc: The pufferfish is a marine fish capable of inflating its body to several times its normal size as a defense mechanism, found in tropical and subtropical waters.

lungfish._en_desc: The lungfish is a freshwater fish with both gills and primitive lungs, one of the closest living relatives to tetrapods found in Africa, South America, and Australia.

coelacanth._en_desc: The coelacanth is a living fossil, a lobe-finned fish once thought extinct that was rediscovered off the coast of South Africa in 1938.

red-bellied-piranha._en_desc: The red-bellied piranha is a freshwater fish native to South America known for its sharp teeth and powerful jaws found in rivers and lakes.

arapaima._en_desc: The arapaima is one of the largest freshwater fish in the world, reaching lengths of over 10 feet, found in the Amazon basin.

piranha._en_desc: The piranha is a freshwater fish native to South American rivers known for its sharp teeth and powerful jaws found in tropical and subtropical waters.

arowana._en_desc: The arowana is a freshwater fish with large, metallic scales and an upward-pointing mouth found in tropical rivers of South America, Asia, and Australia.

electric-eel._en_desc: The electric eel is a freshwater fish capable of generating powerful electric shocks used for hunting and self-defense found in South American rivers.

knifefish._en_desc: The black ghost knifefish is a freshwater fish with an elongated, laterally compressed body and a distinctive anal fin used for propulsion.

betta._en_desc: The betta, or Siamese fighting fish, is a small freshwater fish with flowing fins and vibrant colors native to Southeast Asia.

discus._en_desc: The discus is a freshwater fish with a distinctive disc-shaped body found in the Amazon basin, popular in aquariums for its vibrant colors.

oscarr._en_desc: The oscar is a large cichlid native to South America with a dark body and orange-red markings, popular in aquariums for its personality.

angelfish-freshwater._en_desc: The freshwater angelfish is a popular aquarium fish with a distinctive triangular body shape and long, flowing fins native to the Amazon basin.

convict-cichlid._en_desc: The convict cichlid is a small freshwater fish with distinctive black vertical stripes on a light body found in Central America.

peacock-cichlid._en_desc: The peacock cichlid is a colorful freshwater fish found in Lake Malawi with males displaying vibrant blues, reds, and golds.

lionfish._en_desc: The lionfish is a venomous marine fish with distinctive red, white, and brown stripes and fan-like pectoral fins found in tropical reefs.

stonefish._en_desc: The stonefish is the most venomous fish in the world, masters of camouflage resembling rocks on the ocean floor found in tropical Indo-Pacific waters.

leafy-seadragon._en_desc: The leafy seadragon is a marine fish related to seahorses with leaf-like appendages providing perfect camouflage in kelp forests.

weedy-seadragon._en_desc: The weedy seadragon is a marine fish related to seahorses with small leaf-like appendages found in kelp forests of southern Australia.

boxfish._en_desc: The yellow boxfish is a small, cube-shaped reef fish with bright yellow coloration and black spots found in the Indo-Pacific.

cowfish._en_desc: The longhorn cowfish is a distinctive reef fish with horn-like spines on its head and a boxy, armored body found in tropical Indo-Pacific waters.

trunkfish._en_desc: The spotted trunkfish is a small, box-shaped reef fish with white spots on a dark body found in Caribbean coral reefs.

filefish._en_desc: The scrawled filefish is a marine fish with a distinctive elongated body and blue spots found in tropical Atlantic waters.

triggerfish._en_desc: The queen triggerfish is a large, colorful reef fish with distinctive blue lines on its face and a trigger spine on its dorsal fin.

leatherjacket._en_desc: The slender leatherjacket is a small marine fish with a compressed body and rough skin found in coastal waters worldwide.

parrotfish._en_desc: The stoplight parrotfish is a colorful reef fish with a beak-like mouth used to scrape algae from coral found in Caribbean reefs.

wrasse._en_desc: The cleaner wrasse is a small reef fish with a distinctive blue stripe that sets up cleaning stations to remove parasites from larger fish.

tuskfish._en_desc: The ornate tuskfish is a colorful reef fish with distinctive blue and orange markings found in the Indo-Pacific.

grouper-marbled._en_desc: The marbled grouper is a large reef fish with a marbled pattern found in tropical Indo-Pacific coral reefs.

wrasse-humphead._en_desc: The humphead wrasse is the largest living wrasse species with a distinctive hump on its forehead found in Indo-Pacific coral reefs.

coral-grouper._en_desc: The coral grouper is a large reef fish with a reddish body and blue spots found in tropical Indo-Pacific coral reefs.

cardinalfish._en_desc: The Banggai cardinalfish is a small, striking reef fish with black and white stripes and long fins found only in the Banggai Islands of Indonesia.

damselfish._en_desc: The garibaldi is a bright orange damselfish found in kelp forests of the eastern Pacific, the official marine fish of California.

sergeant-major._en_desc: The sergeant major is a small reef fish with five black vertical bars on a light body found in tropical Atlantic waters.

goby._en_desc: The neon goby is a tiny reef fish with a bright blue stripe that sets up cleaning stations to remove parasites from larger fish.

blenny._en_desc: The Midas blenny is a small, golden-yellow reef fish that mimics cleaner wrasses for protection found in Indo-Pacific coral reefs.

scorpionfish._en_desc: The tasseled scorpionfish is a venomous reef fish with elaborate skin flaps providing excellent camouflage found in tropical Indo-Pacific waters.

flathead._en_desc: The bartail flathead is a bottom-dwelling marine fish with a flattened head and body found in tropical Indo-Pacific waters.

grunt._en_desc: The blue-striped grunt is a small reef fish with distinctive blue horizontal stripes found in Caribbean coral reefs.

tang._en_desc: The clown tang is a bright blue surgeonfish with white and black markings found in coral reefs of the Indo-Pacific.

squirrelfish._en_desc: The squirrelfish is a small, red reef fish with large eyes found in tropical coral reefs worldwide, active at night.

sweep._en_desc: The sweep is a small, silvery fish with a distinctive deep body found in temperate rocky reefs of the Indo-Pacific.

leatherjacket-freshwater._en_desc: The New Zealand magpie is a small freshwater fish with a compressed body and rough skin found in rivers and lakes of New Zealand.

john-dory._en_desc: The John Dory is a marine fish with a distinctive oval body and dark lateral spot found in temperate coastal waters of the Indo-Pacific.

boarfish._en_desc: The longsnout boarfish is a distinctive reef fish with a long, tubular snout and black and white stripes found in tropical Indo-Pacific waters.

bigeye._en_desc: The bigeye is a small reef fish with disproportionately large eyes found in tropical coral reefs worldwide, active at night.

soldierfish._en_desc: The blackbar soldierfish is a small, red reef fish with a distinctive black bar behind its gill cover found in tropical Indo-Pacific waters.

green-anole._en_desc: The green anole is a small arboreal lizard native to the southeastern United States. Often called the American chameleon, it can shift its skin color between green and brown. Males display a pinkish-red dewlap under their throat during courtship or territorial displays.

saltwater-crocodile._en_desc: The saltwater crocodile is the largest living reptile and has the strongest bite force ever measured. Found in coastal regions from eastern India to Australia, it is an opportunistic apex predator. Adults can survive in both saltwater and freshwater environments.

reticulated-python._en_desc: The reticulated python is a non-venomous constrictor and the longest snake in the world. Native to Southeast Asia, it is found in rainforests, rivers, and even near human settlements. It kills prey by constriction and can swallow animals much larger than its head.

panther-chameleon._en_desc: The panther chameleon is a vibrant species native to Madagascar's tropical rainforests. Males display vivid colors ranging from blue, green, and yellow to red. They use their long, sticky tongues to catch insects with remarkable accuracy.

american-alligator._en_desc: The American alligator is a large crocodilian native to the southeastern United States. Once endangered, it has made a remarkable recovery through conservation efforts. It inhabits freshwater environments and is an opportunistic predator of fish, birds, and mammals.

leopard-gecko._en_desc: The leopard gecko is a small, nocturnal lizard native to the rocky deserts and grasslands of South Asia. Unlike many geckos, it has movable eyelids and can blink. It is one of the most popular pet reptiles due to its docile temperament.

eastern-diamondback-rattlesnake._en_desc: The eastern diamondback rattlesnake is the largest venomous snake in North America. Found in the coastal scrublands and pine flatwoods of the southeastern United States, it uses its diamond-shaped dorsal pattern as camouflage. Its rattle serves as an auditory warning to potential threats.

gila-monster._en_desc: The Gila monster is one of only a few venomous lizards in the world, native to the deserts of the southwestern United States and northwestern Mexico. It has a stout body with bead-like scales in black and pink, orange, or yellow patterns. It spends most of its life underground.

leatherback-sea-turtle._en_desc: The leatherback sea turtle is the largest living turtle and the fourth heaviest reptile. Unlike other sea turtles, it has a flexible, leathery carapace instead of a hard shell. It dives to depths exceeding 3,000 feet and feeds almost exclusively on jellyfish.

boomslang._en_desc: The boomslang is a highly venomous rear-fanged snake native to sub-Saharan Africa. Males are typically bright green while females are brown. It is arboreal, spending most of its time in trees, and feeds on birds, chameleons, and small mammals.

indian-cobra._en_desc: The Indian cobra is one of the 'big four' venomous snakes responsible for the most snakebite deaths in India. It is iconic for its hood, which it displays when threatened. It is found across the Indian subcontinent in a variety of habitats.

rhinoceros-iguana._en_desc: The rhinoceros iguana is a large, heavy-bodied lizard endemic to the Caribbean island of Hispaniola. It is named for the bony, horn-like outgrowths on its snout. It inhabits dry, rocky areas and feeds on leaves, flowers, and fruit.

emerald-tree-boa._en_desc: The emerald tree boa is a bright green, non-venomous constrictor native to the rainforests of South America. It spends almost its entire life coiled on branches, waiting to ambush birds and small mammals. Its white markings along the spine help break up its silhouette.

gharial._en_desc: The gharial is a critically endangered crocodilian with a distinctive long, thin snout adapted for catching fish. Once found across the Indian subcontinent, it is now restricted to a few rivers in India and Nepal. It is one of the largest crocodilian species.

mexican-beaded-lizard._en_desc: The Mexican beaded lizard is a large, venomous lizard found in the dry forests and thorn scrub of Mexico and Guatemala. It has black skin with yellow or pinkish banding and bead-like scales. It is nocturnal and spends most of its time in burrows.

desert-tortoise._en_desc: The desert tortoise is a species of tortoise native to the Mojave and Sonoran Deserts. It spends up to 95% of its life underground in burrows that can be over 30 feet long. It is well adapted to extreme heat and arid conditions.

tokay-gecko._en_desc: The tokay gecko is a large gecko native to Southeast Asia, known for its loud, distinctive call. Males are territorial and aggressive, often found on walls and ceilings of buildings. It is widely used in traditional medicine in some Asian cultures.

king-snake._en_desc: The eastern king snake is a powerful, non-venomous constrictor found across the eastern United States. It has a distinctive chain-link pattern of white or yellow bands on a dark background. It is immune to the venom of many pit vipers.

blue-tongued-skink._en_desc: The blue-tongued skink is a group of lizards native to Australia, Tasmania, and New Guinea. They are known for their distinctive blue tongues, which they display as a defense mechanism. They are omnivorous, eating insects, snails, and vegetation.

american-crocodile._en_desc: The American crocodile is found in the coastal regions of the Americas, from southern Florida to northern South America. It is less aggressive than the saltwater crocodile and prefers brackish and saltwater habitats. It is lighter in color than most crocodiles.

asian-water-monitor._en_desc: The Asian water monitor is a large lizard native to Southeast Asia, commonly found near water. It is an opportunistic carnivore feeding on fish, frogs, birds, and carrion. It is one of the most common monitor lizards in the world.

eastern-hognose-snake._en_desc: The eastern hognose snake is a non-venomous colubrid found across eastern North America. It has an upturned snout used for burrowing. When threatened, it may flatten its neck like a cobra or play dead with theatrical drama.

sailfin-lizard._en_desc: The sailfin lizard is a semi-aquatic agamid lizard found in the Philippines and Indonesia. Males have large dorsal crests that resemble sails. They are often found near water and can run bipedally across water surfaces when startled.

texas-rat-snake._en_desc: The Texas rat snake is a large, non-venomous colubrid native to Texas and the south-central United States. It is a powerful constrictor that feeds primarily on rodents. It is highly adaptable and found in a wide range of habitats.

gopher-tortoise._en_desc: The gopher tortoise is a keystone species of the southeastern United States, known for digging extensive burrows. These burrows provide critical shelter for over 350 other species, including the eastern indigo snake. It is a slow-moving herbivore.

bush-viper._en_desc: The bush viper is a venomous, arboreal viper found in the tropical rainforests of equatorial Africa. It has distinctive leaf-shaped, keeled scales in various colors. It is nocturnal and uses its prehensile tail to hang from branches while hunting.

pancake-tortoise._en_desc: The pancake tortoise is a critically endangered species with a uniquely flat, flexible shell. Found in the rocky outcrops of East Africa, it wedges itself into crevices when threatened. It is one of the fastest tortoise species relative to its size.

cottonmouth._en_desc: The cottonmouth, or water moccasin, is a venomous pit viper found in the wetlands of the southeastern United States. It is the only venomous water snake in North America. It is often found swimming with its head above water.

cuban-crocodile._en_desc: The Cuban crocodile is a critically endangered species found only in the Zapata Swamp and Isle of Youth in Cuba. It is highly aggressive and more terrestrial than other crocodiles. It can gallop on land and is known for its distinctive horned ridges.

yellow-bellied-slider._en_desc: The yellow-bellied slider is a semi-aquatic turtle native to the southeastern United States. It has a dark shell with yellow stripes and a distinctive yellow patch on its plastron. It is one of the most common turtle species in pet trade.

western-diamondback-rattlesnake._en_desc: The western diamondback rattlesnake is one of the most dangerous snakes in North America. Found across the southwestern United States and Mexico, it is responsible for the majority of snakebite fatalities in the region. Its rattle serves as a warning when threatened.

caiman-lizard._en_desc: The caiman lizard is a semi-aquatic lizard found in the swamps and rivers of South America. It has a flattened tail for swimming and powerful jaws for crushing snail shells. Its skin resembles that of a caiman, hence its name.

carpet-python._en_desc: The carpet python is a large, non-venomous snake found across Australia and New Guinea. It has a variable pattern of dark bands on a lighter background. It is arboreal and commonly found in trees and on the roofs of houses.

brown-basilisk._en_desc: The brown basilisk is a large lizard found in the tropical rainforests of Central America. It has a distinctive crest on its head and can run bipedally across water. It is semi-arboreal and often found near streams and rivers.

dumerils-boa._en_desc: Dumeril's boa is a heavy-bodied, non-venomous snake endemic to Madagascar. It has a tan and brown pattern that provides excellent camouflage on the forest floor. It is a ground-dwelling ambush predator feeding on mammals and birds.

sulcata-tortoise._en_desc: The African spurred tortoise is the third-largest tortoise species in the world, native to the Sahel region of Africa. It is named for the large, pointed spurs on its legs. It digs deep burrows to escape desert temperatures.

common-caiman._en_desc: The common caiman is a medium-sized crocodilian found throughout Central and South America. It is one of the most widespread crocodilian species. It feeds primarily on fish and invertebrates and is often found in large groups basking on riverbanks.

western-hognose-snake._en_desc: The western hognose snake is a small, non-venomous snake with an upturned snout used for burrowing. Found in the sandy prairies of central North America, it is known for its dramatic threat display. It feeds primarily on toads and small rodents.

forest-cobra._en_desc: The forest cobra is the largest cobra species, found in the tropical forests and savannas of central and western Africa. It is highly venomous and can spit venom accurately. It is a strong swimmer and often found near bodies of water.

veiled-chameleon._en_desc: The veiled chameleon is one of the most popular pet chameleon species, native to Yemen and Saudi Arabia. Males have a distinctive tall casque on their heads. It is an arboreal species that feeds on insects by projecting its long, sticky tongue.

rough-scaled-sand-boa._en_desc: The rough-scaled sand boa is a small, non-venomous constrictor found in the arid deserts of South Asia. It has a stout body adapted for burrowing and spends most of its time beneath the sand. It feeds primarily on rodents and small lizards.

philippine-crocodile._en_desc: The Philippine crocodile is a critically endangered species endemic to the Philippines. It is the most endangered crocodilian in the world, with a wild population estimated at fewer than 100 individuals. It inhabits freshwater rivers, lakes, and marshes.

rainbow-boa._en_desc: The rainbow boa is a non-venomous constrictor found in the rainforests of South America. Its name comes from the iridescent sheen of its scales, which refract light to create a rainbow effect. It is a terrestrial species found on the forest floor.

giant-plated-lizard._en_desc: The giant plated lizard is a large, robust lizard found in the rocky outcrops of southern and eastern Africa. It has heavy, plate-like scales and a powerful tail. It is semi-arboreal and feeds on insects, small vertebrates, and fruit.

black-spiny-tailed-iguana._en_desc: The black spiny-tailed iguana is the fastest lizard in the world, reaching speeds of 21 mph. Native to Central America, it is found on rocky cliffs, walls, and in urban areas. It is an omnivorous species that feeds on plants and small animals.

burmese-python._en_desc: The Burmese python is one of the five largest snakes in the world, native to Southeast Asia. It is a popular pet species but has become a significant invasive species in the Florida Everglades. It is a powerful constrictor that feeds on mammals and birds.

ornate-box-turtle._en_desc: The ornate box turtle is a small, terrestrial turtle native to the prairies of central North America. It has a domed shell with intricate yellow and orange patterns. It can fully close its hinged plastron to protect itself from predators.

common-house-gecko._en_desc: The common house gecko is a small, nocturnal lizard found throughout the tropical and subtropical regions of the world. It is commonly seen on walls and ceilings of buildings, hunting insects. Its toe pads allow it to climb smooth vertical surfaces.

sidewinder-rattlesnake._en_desc: The sidewinder rattlesnake is a venomous pit viper adapted to desert life in the southwestern United States. It uses a distinctive sidewinding locomotion that leaves J-shaped tracks in the sand. It buries itself in sand to ambush prey and escape heat.

chinese-water-dragon._en_desc: The Chinese water dragon is an arboreal agamid lizard found near streams in the forests of southeastern China. Males display vibrant green with white and orange markings. It is an excellent swimmer and can hold its breath for up to an hour.

west-african-dwarf-crocodile._en_desc: The West African dwarf crocodile is the smallest living crocodile species, found in the swamps and rivers of western and central Africa. It is nocturnal and highly terrestrial, digging burrows for shelter. It feeds primarily on fish, crustaceans, and insects.

cape-cobra._en_desc: The Cape cobra is one of the most dangerous cobras in Africa, found in the shrublands and fynbos of southern Africa. It is highly venomous with potent neurotoxin. It is a diurnal species and an excellent climber.

crested-iguana._en_desc: The crested iguana is a critically endangered species endemic to the dry forests of western Madagascar. It has a distinctive high dorsal crest and is one of the rarest iguanas in the world. It is primarily herbivorous, feeding on leaves and fruit.

argentine-tegu._en_desc: The Argentine black and white tegu is a large, omnivorous lizard native to South America. It has distinctive black and white banding and a robust body. It feeds on a wide variety of foods including insects, small animals, fruit, and eggs.

king-brown-snake._en_desc: The king brown snake, also known as the mulga snake, is one of Australia's most widespread and dangerous snakes. Despite its name, it belongs to the black snake genus Pseudechis. It is responsible for more snakebite deaths in Australia than any other species.

false-gharial._en_desc: The false gharial is a critically endangered crocodilian found in the rivers and swamps of Southeast Asia. It has a distinctive long, narrow snout and is one of the largest crocodilian species. It is a specialist fish-eater with a unique jaw structure.

indian-star-tortoise._en_desc: The Indian star tortoise is a small to medium-sized tortoise native to India and Sri Lanka. It has distinctive star-shaped patterns on its carapace that radiate from the center of each scute. It is a popular species in the illegal pet trade.

green-anaconda._en_desc: The green anaconda is the heaviest and one of the longest snakes in the world, found in the swamps and rivers of South America. It is a non-venomous constrictor that feeds on deer, capybaras, and even jaguars. It spends most of its time in water.

tuatara._en_desc: The tuatara is a reptile endemic to New Zealand and the only surviving member of the order Rhynchocephalia. Often called a living fossil, it has remained virtually unchanged for 200 million years. It has a third eye on top of its head that detects light changes.

eastern-water-dragon._en_desc: The eastern water dragon is a large agamid lizard found along rivers and creeks in eastern Australia. Males have a distinctive red chest and a spiny crest along their back. It is semi-aquatic and an excellent swimmer.

spider-tortoise._en_desc: The spider tortoise is a critically endangered species endemic to the dry spiny forests of southern Madagascar. It has distinctive yellow radiating patterns on its dark shell that resemble a spider's web. It is one of the smallest tortoise species in the world.

russian-tortoise._en_desc: The Russian tortoise is a small species native to the arid steppes of Central Asia. It is one of the most cold-tolerant tortoise species, surviving harsh winters by brumating underground. It is popular in the pet trade due to its small size and hardy nature.

cat-eyed-snake._en_desc: The cat-eyed snake is a small, rear-fanged snake found in the tropical rainforests of Central and South America. It has distinctive vertical pupils and is primarily nocturnal. It feeds on frogs, lizards, and small mammals.

arabian-chameleon._en_desc: The Arabian chameleon is a species of chameleon native to the Arabian Peninsula. It is adapted to arid conditions, unlike most chameleon species. It has a casque on its head and can change color for communication and thermoregulation.

spotted-turtle._en_desc: The spotted turtle is one of the smallest turtles in North America, found in shallow, slow-moving waters. It has a smooth, dark shell with distinctive yellow or orange spots. It is a long-lived species that can survive for over a century.

banded-krait._en_desc: The banded krait is a highly venomous elapid found in South and Southeast Asia. It has distinctive black and yellow bands and is primarily nocturnal. It feeds on other snakes, including venomous species, and is responsible for many snakebite deaths in Asia.

golden-skink._en_desc: The golden skink is a small, fast-moving lizard found in tropical forests and gardens across South and Southeast Asia. It has a metallic, iridescent body that gives it a golden appearance. It is diurnal and feeds on insects and small invertebrates.

broad-snouted-caiman._en_desc: The broad-snouted caiman is a medium-sized crocodilian found in the freshwater habitats of South America. It has a broad, flat snout adapted for catching fish and invertebrates. It builds vegetation mounds to incubate its eggs.

copperhead._en_desc: The copperhead is a venomous pit viper found across the eastern United States. It has a distinctive copper-colored head and hourglass-shaped crossbands. It is responsible for the most snakebite cases in North America, though fatalities are rare.

radiated-tortoise._en_desc: The radiated tortoise is a critically endangered species endemic to Madagascar. It has a high-domed shell with striking yellow star-shaped patterns radiating from the center of each scute. It is threatened by habitat loss and poaching for food and the pet trade.

blue-racer._en_desc: The blue racer is a fast-moving, non-venomous colubrid found across the central United States and southern Ontario. It has a distinctive blue-grey dorsal color and a white or cream underside. It is diurnal and feeds on rodents, frogs, and other snakes.

side-blotched-lizard._en_desc: The side-blotched lizard is a small lizard found in the deserts and grasslands of western North America. It is famous in evolutionary biology for its rock-paper-scissors mating strategy. Males have three throat colors that correspond to different mating tactics.

nile-monitor._en_desc: The Nile monitor is a large, powerful lizard found throughout sub-Saharan Africa near water. It is semi-aquatic and feeds on fish, frogs, birds, eggs, and carrion. It has a forked tongue used for detecting prey in the water.

canebrake-rattlesnake._en_desc: The canebrake rattlesnake, a subspecies of the timber rattlesnake, is found in the forests and swamps of the southeastern United States. It has a distinctive pinkish-brown color with dark crossbands. It is a dangerous venomous pit viper.

yellow-footed-tortoise._en_desc: The yellow-footed tortoise is a medium-sized tortoise native to the Amazon Basin of South America. It has distinctive yellow or orange scales on its legs and head. It feeds primarily on fallen fruit and plays an important ecological role in seed dispersal.

puff-adder._en_desc: The puff adder is a venomous viper found throughout sub-Saharan Africa. It relies on its excellent camouflage and will not flee when approached, leading to many defensive strikes. It is an ambush predator that strikes with incredible speed.

eastern-green-mamba._en_desc: The eastern green mamba is a fast, highly venomous elapid found in the coastal forests of eastern and southern Africa. It is bright green, blending perfectly with the forest canopy. Unlike the black mamba, it is arboreal and rarely comes to the ground.

cape-dwarf-chameleon._en_desc: The Cape dwarf chameleon is a small chameleon endemic to the Western Cape of South Africa. It has independently rotating eyes, a prehensile tail, and a long, sticky tongue for catching insects. It can change color for communication and thermoregulation.

chinese-alligator._en_desc: The Chinese alligator is a critically endangered species, one of only two alligator species in the world. Found in eastern China, it is smaller than the American alligator and has bony plates on its eyelids. Wild populations are critically low.

snouted-cobra._en_desc: The snouted cobra is a large, highly venomous snake found across southern Africa. It has a distinctive upturned snout and can spit venom accurately. It is found in a wide variety of habitats and feeds on rodents, birds, and other snakes.

common-wall-lizard._en_desc: The common wall lizard is a small, agile lizard found across Europe and introduced to North America. It is commonly seen basking on stone walls and buildings. It feeds on insects, spiders, and small invertebrates.

brown-tree-snake._en_desc: The brown tree snake is an arboreal, rear-fanged snake native to Australia and New Guinea. It has become one of the world's most destructive invasive species on Guam, where it has eliminated most of the island's native bird species. It is nocturnal and feeds on birds, lizards, and mammals.

angulate-tortoise._en_desc: The angulate tortoise is a small tortoise found in the fynbos and karoo shrublands of southern Africa. It has a distinctive upturned front margin to its shell. It is well adapted to the Mediterranean climate of the Western Cape region.

savannah-monitor._en_desc: The savannah monitor is a medium-sized monitor lizard found across sub-Saharan Africa. It is a ground-dwelling species that digs burrows for shelter. It feeds on insects, small mammals, and reptiles, and is popular in the exotic pet trade.

white-lipped-pit-viper._en_desc: The white-lipped pit viper is a venomous snake found in the tropical rainforests of Southeast Asia. It has a distinctive white or yellow line along its upper lip and is primarily arboreal. It is a nocturnal ambush predator that feeds on rodents and birds.

alabama-red-bellied-cooter._en_desc: The Alabama red-bellied cooter is an endangered freshwater turtle endemic to Alabama and Georgia. It has a dark shell with a distinctive red or orange plastron. It is found in rivers, lakes, and ponds with abundant aquatic vegetation.

amazon-tree-boa._en_desc: The Amazon tree boa is a small, arboreal constrictor found throughout the Amazon rainforest. It is nocturnal and feeds on birds and small mammals. It has an extremely variable color pattern, ranging from yellow to red to brown.

california-kingsnake._en_desc: The California kingsnake is a popular, non-venomous constrictor found across the western United States. It has a banded pattern of brown and white or yellow. It is an opportunistic feeder that readily eats rattlesnakes, making it beneficial to humans.

clouded-monitor._en_desc: The clouded monitor is a medium-sized monitor lizard found in the tropical rainforests of Southeast Asia. It is arboreal and has a long, slender body adapted for climbing. It feeds on insects, small mammals, and birds.

brazilian-rainbow-boa._en_desc: The Brazilian rainbow boa is a medium-sized, non-venomous constrictor found in the rainforests of South America. Its name comes from the stunning iridescent sheen of its scales. It is primarily terrestrial and feeds on rodents, birds, and bats.

northern-cuirassated-lizard._en_desc: The northern cuirassated lizard is a small lizard found in the rocky hillsides of Mexico. It has distinctive bony armor plates called osteoderms covering its body. It is diurnal and feeds on insects and small invertebrates.

desert-iguana._en_desc: The desert iguana is a medium-sized lizard found in the deserts of the southwestern United States and northwestern Mexico. It is one of the most heat-tolerant lizards, active at temperatures that force other reptiles to seek shade. It feeds primarily on leaves and flowers.

false-water-cobra._en_desc: The false water cobra is a large, semi-aquatic colubrid found in the wetlands of South America. It displays a cobra-like hood when threatened, despite being only mildly venomous. It is an excellent swimmer and feeds on fish, frogs, and small mammals.

garter-snake._en_desc: The common garter snake is one of the most widespread snakes in North America, found in gardens, meadows, and woodlands. It has distinctive longitudinal stripes. Despite being mildly venomous, it is harmless to humans and beneficial as pest control.

shingleback-skink._en_desc: The shingleback skink is a large, slow-moving lizard found in the woodlands and grasslands of southern Australia. It has rough, pinecone-like scales and a short, fat tail that resembles its head, confusing predators. It is one of the few reptile species that mate for life.

mozambique-spitting-cobra._en_desc: The Mozambique spitting cobra is a highly venomous elapid found across eastern and southern Africa. It is one of the most dangerous snakes in the region, responsible for many snakebite cases. It can spit venom accurately into the eyes of perceived threats.

american-bullfrog._en_desc: The American Bullfrog is the largest frog in North America. They are powerful swimmers and aggressive predators, known for their deep jug-o-rum calls that can be heard up to a mile away.

glass-frog._en_desc: Glass Frogs are remarkable amphibians with translucent ventral skin. Found in Central and South America, they spend most of their lives in trees and descend only to breed near fast-flowing streams.

pacman-frog._en_desc: The Pacman Frog, also known as the Argentine Horned Frog, is a popular pet species known for its large mouth and sedentary lifestyle. They are ambush predators that sit and wait for prey to pass by.

budgetts-frog._en_desc: Budgett's Frog is a flattened, broad-bodied frog found in South America. They are known for their aggressive defensive behavior, including inflating, screaming, and biting when disturbed.

whites-tree-frog._en_desc: White's Tree Frog, also known as the Dumpy Tree Frog, is one of the most docile and popular amphibian pets. Native to Australia and New Guinea, they are known for their placid temperament and ability to thrive in captivity.

african-dwarf-frog._en_desc: African Dwarf Frogs are tiny, fully aquatic amphibians that never leave the water. They are social creatures that do best in groups and are popular aquarium pets due to their small size and active nature.

amazon-milk-frog._en_desc: The Amazon Milk Frog is a large tree frog found in the Amazon rainforest. They have a distinctive black and white or blue and white banded pattern and are named for the milky toxic substance they secrete.

gray-tree-frog._en_desc: The Gray Tree Frog is a small, arboreal frog native to eastern North America. They have bumpy skin that resembles tree bark and bright yellow-orange patches on the inside of their hind legs.

spring-peeper._en_desc: Spring Peepers are tiny tree frogs whose chorus marks the arrival of spring in eastern North America. Their characteristic X-shaped marking on their back helps identify them among other small frogs.

wood-frog._en_desc: Wood Frogs are remarkable for their ability to freeze during winter and thaw out alive in spring. Found across North America, they have a distinctive dark mask marking behind each eye.

american-toad._en_desc: The American Toad is one of the most common and widespread toads in North America. They have warty skin, parotoid glands that produce a mild toxin, and can live for over a decade in the wild.

cane-toad._en_desc: The Cane Toad is a large, toxic toad native to Central and South America. It has become one of the most successful invasive amphibians, spreading across Australia, the Caribbean, and Pacific islands.

fire-bellied-toad._en_desc: Fire-Bellied Toads are small, semi-aquatic toads with bumpy olive-green backs and vivid orange or red bellies. They are popular pets and are known for their aposematic coloration that warns predators of their toxins.

desert-rain-frog._en_desc: The Desert Rain Frog is a tiny, round frog that burrows into sand along the coast of South Africa and Namibia. They spend most of their lives underground and emerge only to feed and breed during foggy conditions.

goliath-frog._en_desc: The Goliath Frog, or Conraua goliath, is the world's largest frog. Found only in Cameroon and Equatorial Guinea, these massive amphibians inhabit fast-flowing rivers and are threatened by habitat loss and hunting.

mountain-chicken-frog._en_desc: The Mountain Chicken Frog is one of the largest frogs in the Caribbean, found only on Dominica and Montserrat. They are critically endangered due to the chytrid fungus and habitat destruction.

spadefoot-toad._en_desc: Spadefoot Toads are adapted to arid environments with specialized keratinized spades on their hind feet for burrowing. They spend most of their lives underground and breed explosively in temporary rain pools.

natterjack-toad._en_desc: The Natterjack Toad is a medium-sized toad found across Europe. Unlike most toads, they run rather than hop and are known for their loud, rasping calls during breeding season.

midwife-toad._en_desc: Midwife Toads are small, nocturnal toads named for the male's paternal behavior of carrying eggs on his hind legs. Found across Europe, they have a distinctive high-pitched beep-like call.

european-tree-frog._en_desc: The European Tree Frog is a small, bright green frog with a distinctive dark stripe along each side. They are excellent climbers and are often found in gardens, orchards, and damp woodlands.

leopard-frog._en_desc: The Leopard Frog gets its name from the distinctive dark spots covering its green or brown body. Found across North America, they are strong jumpers and swimmers that inhabit a variety of wetland habitats.

strawberry-poison-dart-frog._en_desc: The Strawberry Poison Dart Frog, also known as the Blue Jeans Frog, is a small but vividly colored amphibian found in Central America. Males carry tadpoles on their backs to suitable pools of water.

dyeing-poison-dart-frog._en_desc: The Dyeing Poison Dart Frog is a variable species with striking color patterns. Found in South America, they were named for the use of their skin secretions by indigenous peoples to dye feathers and textiles.

harlequin-toad._en_desc: Harlequin Toads are a diverse group of brightly colored toads found in Central and South America. Many species are critically endangered or believed extinct due to the chytrid fungus and habitat loss.

pickerel-frog._en_desc: The Pickerel Frog is a brownish frog with two parallel rows of dark rectangular spots down its back. Found in eastern North America, they are one of the few frogs whose skin secretions are toxic to other amphibians.

cherry-tree-frog._en_desc: The Cherry Tree Frog is a small European tree frog known for its distinctive call that sounds like a cherry pit being clicked. They are excellent climbers with adhesive toe pads.

asian-common-toad._en_desc: The Asian Common Toad is a widespread toad found across South and Southeast Asia. They are highly adaptable to urban environments and are often found in gardens, drains, and agricultural areas.

clown-tree-frog._en_desc: The Clown Tree Frog is a colorful, medium-sized tree frog found in the Amazon rainforest. They have striking patterns of brown, green, and cream that provide excellent camouflage against tree bark.

gliding-tree-frog._en_desc: The Gliding Tree Frog has evolved enlarged adhesive toe pads and partially webbed feet that allow it to glide through the rainforest canopy. Found in Central America, they are active at night.

black-legged-poison-frog._en_desc: The Black-Legged Poison Frog is a small, toxic frog found in the rainforests of Colombia. They are known for their complex parental care behaviors and striking black and yellow coloration.

red-backed-poison-frog._en_desc: The Red-Backed Poison Frog is a small, brightly colored amphibian found in the Amazon rainforest. Their vivid red or orange back serves as a warning to potential predators.

splashback-poison-frog._en_desc: The Splashback Poison Frog is a small amphibian with vivid coloration that varies from green to blue to yellow. Found in South America, they carry tadpoles on their backs to water-filled bromeliads.

cane-turtle-frog._en_desc: The Cane Turtle Frog is a small, flattened frog found in South America. They are often found in agricultural areas, particularly sugarcane fields, and have a distinctive flattened appearance.

malaysian-horned-frog._en_desc: The Malaysian Horned Frog is a medium-sized frog with distinctive horn-like projections above each eye. Found in Southeast Asian rainforests, they are well-camouflaged among dead leaves on the forest floor.

hampire-poison-dart-frog._en_desc: The Hamphire Poison Dart Frog is a small, strikingly colored amphibian found in South America. Their bold pattern serves as a warning to predators of their toxic skin secretions.

brazilian-horned-frog._en_desc: The Brazilian Horned Frog is a medium-sized frog with horn-like projections above its eyes. Found in the Amazon rainforest, they are well-camouflaged and lie in wait to ambush passing prey.

hairy-frog._en_desc: The Hairy Frog, also known as the Trichobatrachus, is a unique amphibian found in Central Africa. Males develop hair-like dermal papillae on their flanks and thighs during the breeding season.

tomato-frog._en_desc: The Tomato Frog is a bright red-orange frog found in Madagascar. When threatened, they inflate their bodies and secrete a sticky white substance that can temporarily immobilize predators.

marsupial-frog._en_desc: The Marsupial Frog is a remarkable amphibian found in the Andes mountains. Females have a dorsal pouch where they carry their eggs until they develop into froglets, bypassing the tadpole stage.

foam-nest-frog._en_desc: Foam Nest Frogs are found across Africa and South America. They are named for their unique breeding behavior where both sexes whip up a foam nest to protect their eggs from drying out.

surinam-toad._en_desc: The Surinam Toad is a flat, bottom-dwelling amphibian found in South America. Females have a remarkable reproductive strategy where eggs are embedded in the skin of their backs until they emerge as fully formed froglets.

axolotl._en_desc: The Axolotl is a neotenic salamander that retains its larval features throughout life, including external gills. Found only in Lake Xochimilco in Mexico, it is critically endangered in the wild but widely bred in captivity.

tiger-salamander._en_desc: The Tiger Salamander is the largest terrestrial salamander in North America. They have distinctive yellow or olive markings on a dark background and spend most of their lives underground in burrows.

eastern-newt._en_desc: The Eastern Newt has a complex life cycle with three distinct stages: aquatic larva, terrestrial red eft, and aquatic adult. Found in eastern North America, they produce tetrodotoxin in their skin.

hellbender._en_desc: The Hellbender is the largest salamander in North America, reaching up to two feet long. Found in clean, fast-flowing streams of the eastern United States, they are declining due to pollution and habitat loss.

olm._en_desc: The Olm is a blind, cave-dwelling salamander found in the caves of southern Europe. It has no eyes, is depigmented, and can live for over 100 years, making it one of the longest-lived vertebrates.

fire-salamander._en_desc: The Fire Salamander is one of Europe's most recognizable amphibians with its striking black body and bright yellow or orange markings. Found in central and southern Europe, they secrete samandarin, a neurotoxin.

spotted-salamander._en_desc: The Spotted Salamander is a large, robust salamander found in eastern North America. They have distinctive yellow spots on a dark background and are one of the few vertebrates known to have algae living inside their cells.

red-backed-salamander._en_desc: The Red-Backed Salamander is the most common and abundant salamander in eastern North America. They are entirely lungless, breathing through their moist skin, and come in both red-backed and lead-backed color phases.

mudpuppy._en_desc: The Mudpuppy is a fully aquatic salamander found in eastern North America. They retain their bushy red external gills throughout life and are nocturnal hunters that use sensory barbels to find prey.
